21 unchanged paragraphs, under In short {#in-short}, The bookmarklet that out-designed the application {#story}, Every site still fights its readers {#problems}…

My argument is simple. The next generation of user experience is the one the user customises: the reading mode, the layout, the contrast, the things hidden and the things kept, set by the person reading, for themselves. And then, as I argued in [Software vendors should become villagers and town planners](../../software-vendors-as-villagers.md), it is the one they pay for, so that somebody else keeps their customisation working through every release. I do not want to maintain my fixes. I wantwould like to make them, and pay someone to keep them alive.
